Clicking Silence in AlertRuleMenu sets showSilenceDrawer to true, but the drawer is only rendered when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. In the list view `rule` is undefined while the Prometheus-based ability still makes the Silence menu item visible, so clicking Silence opens nothing and the user cannot create a silence from the list view.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the Silence menu item is shown based on Prom abilities, but the drawer only renders when a Grafana ruler rule exists. In list views the rule is undefined, so clicking Silence does nothing.

false_positives.candidate:
Pause action is never shown in the ruler-free list view

The pause menu item requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) in addition to canPause. In the new list view rulerRule is intentionally undefined, so even though the Grafana Prometheus ability can set canPause to true, the Pause/Unpause item is never rendered there. Users can no longer pause or resume Grafana rules from the list view.

Delete action is never shown in the ruler-free list view

The Delete menu item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the new list view rulerRule is undefined, so the newly added Grafana Prometheus delete ability has no effect and users with delete permission cannot delete a Grafana rule from the list's More menu. The underlying delete handler in RuleActionsButtons.V2 operates on the rule identifier and does not need the ruler rule object.

skipToken does not neutralize the Duplicate ability for non-Grafana rules

useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities converts skipToken to undefined, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities treats an undefined rule as supported because useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading=false for no rule. Duplicate therefore becomes [AlwaysSupported, grafana AlertingRuleCreate permission]. When AlertRuleMenu renders a cloud/data-source rule, a user who has Grafana rule-create permission but not the external rule-create permission incorrectly gets the Duplicate action via the OR of ruler and Grafana abilities.

Combined-rule abilities no longer treat federated groups as immutable

useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and marked rules in federated groups as not supported for update/delete/pause-type actions. The refactored useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated to false, so federated Mimir rule groups can now appear editable/removable in consumers using CombinedRule abilities, regressing the previous protection for federated groups.

Grafana recording rules lose pause and export abilities

The Prometheus-based abilities gate Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently, and ModifyExport on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). The ruler-based path used isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, which includes Grafana recording rules as well as alerting rules. As a result, Grafana recording rules in the ruler-free list view cannot be paused or exported even though those actions were supported for them through the ruler-based path.

Grafana rule link drops the returnTo parameter

The deleted GrafanaRuleListItem built its view href with createReturnTo() so the rule detail view received a returnTo query parameter pointing back to the current list context. The new component links directly to /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view without returnTo, so navigation back from a rule opened from the filtered/group list loses the list context that the previous link explicitly preserved.

Menu test codifies the missing Delete item instead of covering it

The test grants AlertingRuleDelete globally and in folder access control and defines a delete menu selector, but the More-menu test expects exactly four menu items and never asserts Delete. This hides the regression that Delete is not rendered in the ruler-free Grafana list even for users with delete permission.

Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting can defeat the $__range split guard

runSplitQuery() now replaces template variables in query.expr at line 299 and only afterwards, at line 300, partitions queries with querySupportsSplitting(). That helper is documented at lines 282-288 to keep queries containing $__range, $__range_s or $__range_ms out of splitting so the backend can interpolate the range against the unsplit time range. If applyTemplateVariables() substitutes those range variables (as it does other variables such as $__auto/$step in the new test), the marker is gone before the check, the query is classified as splittable, and every time chunk is sent with the range value frozen from the original panel range, producing incorrect rate/range results instead of the intended single unsplit request. The splittability check needs to be done on the pre-interpolation expression or range variables must be provably preserved and covered by a test.

Shard-split queries are interpolated twice, once per shard group

runShardSplitQuery() interpolates every target with datasource.applyTemplateVariables() at line 52, adds the __stream_shard__ selector, and then delegates each shard group to runSplitQuery() (line 163), which after this change interpolates the same targets again at querySplitting.ts:299. The updated test codifies this: a single target now triggers applyTemplateVariables 5 times (1 initial + 1 per shard sub-request). Template interpolation with scopedVars and ad-hoc filters (request.filters is passed in both places) is not a guaranteed idempotent operation: variable values containing '$', $__auto/step derivation, and ad-hoc filter injection into the stream selector can be applied a second time to an already interpolated/shard-augmented expression, and the redundant work scales with the number of shard groups. runSplitQuery needs a way for the shard path to skip re-interpolation, or the shard path should not pre-interpolate beyond what shard grouping requires.

Empty-expression filtering now happens before interpolation in shard splitting

The filters at lines 50-51 run before the interpolation map at line 52, whereas the previous code interpolated first and then dropped queries with no expr. A target whose expr is only a template variable (e.g. expr: '$q') that expands to an empty string now passes the filter, is interpolated to '', and continues into groupTargetsByQueryType()/getSelectorForShardValues() and on to execution as an empty LogQL query instead of being ignored, causing shard-label fetching and/or a Loki parse error for a query that should have been dropped. The expr emptiness check should also (or instead) be applied to the interpolated result; the same filter-before-map pattern was introduced in runSplitQuery at querySplitting.ts:296-299.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Device limit is enforced by a non-atomic count-then-insert and can be exceeded concurrently

CreateOrUpdateDevice runs CountDevices in one DB session and, if the count is below the limit, performs the INSERT/UPSERT in a separate session with no transaction, lock, or other serialization. Concurrent first-time requests for distinct devices (across goroutines or Grafana instances sharing the database) can all observe count == limit-1 and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. The check-and-create needs to be atomic, e.g. inside a transaction with appropriate locking.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same race condition: a non-atomic device count check followed by an insert lets concurrent requests exceed the device limit. Both also suggest a transaction or lock as the fix.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateDevice can falsely report the limit reached for an existing MySQL device

updateDevice treats RowsAffected == 0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL, RowsAffected for UPDATE counts changed rows, not matched rows; when an already-known device is re-tagged (e.g. via another instance whose local cache is cold) within the same second and with unchanged client_ip/user_agent, the stored updated_at has second precision so nothing changes and MySQL reports 0. A legitimate, already-counted device is then denied as if it were new. Use a matched-row check (existence SELECT, or found-rows semantics) instead of relying on changed-row counts.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to updateDevice wrongly mapping RowsAffected == 0 to ErrDeviceLimitReached. The golden comment says zero rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window. The candidate gives a different cause, MySQL's changed-rows semantics, but flags the same faulty logic in the same function.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Failed device-limit check poisons the local cache and lets the device in on retry

tagDeviceUI writes the device key to localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and never removes it when that call fails. A new device over the limit is denied on its first request, but the cache entry remains for the 29-minute cache TTL; on its next request tagDeviceUI returns nil on the cache hit without touching the store, TagDevice returns nil, and Anonymous.Authenticate grants an identity. The configured limit is therefore bypassed after a single denied attempt on the same instance. Set the cache entry only after a successful store write, or delete it when CreateOrUpdateDevice returns an error.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug. tagDeviceUI writes the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs, and the entry is not removed when the device limit is hit. Later requests then bypass the limit until the 29-minute TTL expires.

false_positives.candidate:
Provider signature changes are not reflected in wire generation, breaking the server build

ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB instead of anonstore.AnonStore and constructs the store itself, and ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit that wire cannot supply. The checked-in pkg/server/wire_gen.go is not updated in this PR and still calls both providers with their old signatures, so the server package will not compile; the wire provider set also still needs to drop/replace ProvideAnonDBStore and be regenerated.

Anonymous authentication now blocks on the database with no timeout or panic isolation

Authenticate previously tagged the device in a goroutine with a 2-minute background-context timeout and panic recovery; it now calls TagDevice synchronously with the request context and no deadline. A slow or stalled device-store query (count plus upsert, now on the auth path) blocks anonymous authentication indefinitely, a client disconnect cancels the tagging via the request context, and a panic in tagging now propagates into authentication. Keep the synchronous enforcement needed for the limit, but bound it with a timeout context and recover from panics.

No test covers an existing device updating successfully while at the limit, or client-level denial

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only verifies that a second, new device is rejected when the limit is 1. The other half of the feature branch—an already-registered device calling CreateOrUpdateDevice again while count >= limit must succeed via updateDevice—is untested, as is Anonymous.Authenticate returning an error (and no identity) on ErrDeviceLimitReached and unlimited behavior with limit 0 end to end (impl_test.go always uses a default cfg with limit 0). A regression in updateDevice would ship undetected.

New device_limit option is not added to default configuration or documentation

The PR reads [auth.anonymous] device_limit into Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit but does not add it to conf/defaults.ini (or the configuration documentation). Operators have no discoverable way to learn the option exists or that 0 means unlimited and negative values are also treated as unlimited by the deviceLimit > 0 guard. Add the setting with its default and semantics to defaults.ini and the auth.anonymous docs.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales are loaded only during web requests

I18n.translate loads only config.locale before delegating to the backend, while the new code loads the site-default and English fallback files only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, console code, and model-level translations therefore query fallback locales whose YAML files were never loaded and receive 'translation missing'. Worse, argument-less lookups cache that missing result in the LRU cache at lines 71-76, so the missing string can persist after a later web request loads the fallback locale. Fallback loading belongs in the translation/load path, not only in the controller.

Every fallback lookup depends on SiteSetting and can fail outside a ready request stack

FallbackLocaleList#[] unconditionally calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, and I18n::Backend::Fallbacks invokes this method for translation misses in any context, not just after ApplicationController has already resolved the locale. If the setting is blank or the settings/DB layer is unavailable during boot, migrations, seeding, or job startup, a routine missing translation becomes a NoMethodError or database error instead of falling back to :en. The hot missing-translation path should use a guarded or cached default that safely degrades to English.

Cached translations ignore the dynamic fallback chain

The LRU cache key contains only the key, current locale, and backend object_id, but after this change the result for a key missing in the current locale also depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, which FallbackLocaleList reads dynamically. Changing the site default locale does not change the cache key or clear the cache, so users can keep receiving text in the previous fallback language until entries are evicted or translations are manually reloaded.

No tests cover the new fallback behaviour

The pull request introduces a custom FallbackLocaleList, backend Fallbacks inclusion, fallback-file loading, and a controller hook, but adds no specs. There is no coverage proving that a key missing in the user locale resolves first to the site default and then to English, that fallback locale files are loaded before lookup, or that pluralized/interpolated fallback translations work, so regressions would silently surface as 'translation missing' text.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

true_positives.golden_comment: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
TestLogger.FromContext discards recorded logs

FromContext returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of the receiver or a logger sharing the receiver's recording state. LoggerMiddleware now logs through m.logger.FromContext(ctx), so a test that constructs it with a TestLogger and then inspects that original fake will always see zero InfoLogs and cannot verify the "Plugin Request Completed" log; the log is written to a discarded instance. FromContext should return the receiver (or a derived logger sharing the same Logs state).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug. TestLogger.FromContext returns a new instance instead of the receiver, so logs land on a discarded instance and test assertions against the original logger break.

false_positives.candidate:
No test covers contextual-logger propagation to LoggerMiddleware

This PR moves instrumentContext into a new middleware and makes LoggerMiddleware depend on it (it now obtains pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname only via logger.FromContext(ctx) instead of explicit log parameters), but no test is added for ContextualLoggerMiddleware and the renamed metrics test only asserts Prometheus metrics. Add a test that runs ContextualLoggerMiddleware before LoggerMiddleware and asserts the emitted log carries the contextual attributes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes when host is nil

The callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!, and the model has no presence validation. Creating or updating a record without a host (reachable through the new admin API by omitting embeddable_host.host) raises NoMethodError before validates_format_of can produce a validation error, turning bad input into a 500. The handler should parse discourseUrl, extract its exact origin, and require strict equality with e.origin.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same problem: the postMessage origin check uses indexOf substring matching, which is insufficient and can be bypassed. They give different bypass examples, but the underlying flaw and the fix (strict origin equality) are the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported URL is interpolated unescaped into stored HTML

TopicEmbed.import builds the 'Imported from' anchor by inserting the supplied URL directly into an HTML string, both as the href attribute value and as the link text. The only earlier check is that the string starts with http:// or https://, so a URL containing quotes or angle brackets can break out of the anchor and inject arbitrary markup. Because the resulting post uses raw_html rendering, that injected markup is stored and served without sanitization. The URL and link text must be HTML/attribute escaped, or the anchor must be built with a DOM builder.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment raises two issues: a NoMethodError on nil contents, and XSS from unescaped URL interpolation. The candidate identifies the XSS part precisely: the URL is placed unescaped into the anchor's href and link text, then rendered as raw HTML. That is a core part of the golden comment, though the candidate does not mention the nil contents error.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed polling crashes on items without full content

poll_feed unconditionally calls i.content.scrub for every feed item. Many RSS/Atom items provide only a description or summary and no content/content:encoded element, in which case i.content is nil and this raises NoMethodError. The job is configured with retry: false and has no per-item error handling, so one such item aborts the entire hourly import and prevents all remaining items from being processed. The code should fall back to description/summary when content is absent and isolate failures per item.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: i.content.scrub is called when i.content can be nil, causing a crash. Both also propose falling back to description. The candidate adds detail about retry and per-item isolation, but the core issue is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
Raw-HTML posts bypass HTML sanitization

Post#cook returns the stored raw text verbatim for the new raw_html cook method, and TopicEmbed uses that method for imported content. The feed-polling path passes arbitrary RSS/Atom HTML directly to TopicEmbed without Readability's tag whitelist or any other sanitizer, after which the result is stored as cooked HTML and rendered raw. A malicious or compromised feed item containing script tags, event-handler attributes, or other active markup therefore becomes stored XSS for forum visitors. Imported HTML must be passed through a whitelist sanitizer before it is saved as cooked content.

Remote import performs unrestricted server-side fetching

TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read before TopicEmbed.import performs its scheme check, with no timeout, response-size limit, or restriction on redirect targets or private IP addresses. The on-demand retrieval flow validates only the initial URL's host, while open-uri follows HTTP redirects, so an embeddable-host URL can redirect the server to localhost, link-local, or internal services and have the fetched content converted into a public topic; a very large response is also read entirely into memory. Fetching needs an explicit HTTP(S) client with scheme/final-URI validation, private-address blocking, timeouts, and a size cap.

Unknown embed URLs enqueue unbounded background jobs

Every request for an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job, and the loading page automatically reloads and repeats the request. The Referer check is trivially spoofable by non-browser clients, and TopicRetriever's 60-second throttle is only applied after a job is dequeued, so an attacker can flood Sidekiq with jobs and use distinct URLs on the embeddable host to trigger repeated outbound fetch attempts. Host validation and an atomic throttle/deduplication check need to happen before enqueueing, with throttled requests returning the loading response without creating another job.

Embed creation has a check-then-create race

TopicEmbed.import first queries for an existing embed and then creates the topic, post, and embed record without any locking. The scheduled feed poller and an on-demand RetrieveTopic job (or two concurrent retrieves) can both observe no embed for the same URL and both create content; the loser then hits the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url at create! and the whole job fails with RecordNotUnique even though the URL was successfully imported by the winner. Creation should be made atomic or rescue RecordNotUnique and return the existing embed's post.

Disqus import now depends on live thread URLs and drops the category option

The importer previously created each topic locally from the Disqus export, but now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which fetches t[:link] over the network for every thread. If a linked article has moved, returns 404, or the import runs offline, open() raises and aborts the entire import, losing comments that are fully present in the export file. The same change removes the --category Thor option, breaking existing import invocations that pass it and leaving no way to place imported threads in a category. The export-based creation needs to remain as a fallback and the category option needs to be plumbed through to topic creation.

Only root-relative URLs are absolutized in imported content

absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values that start with '/'. Relative references such as 'images/photo.jpg' or 'page2.html', which are common in feed content, are left unchanged and will resolve against the Discourse host instead of the source article, producing broken images and links. Conversely, a protocol-relative URL like '//cdn.example.com/x.js' starts with '/' and is incorrectly rewritten onto the article's host. All non-absolute references should be resolved with URI.join against the source URL, which handles relative, root-relative, and protocol-relative forms correctly.

Feed-setting guard specs pass without exercising the guards

The specs for 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' stub only the setting named in the example. Jobs::PollFeed#execute checks feed_polling_enabled? first, and that setting defaults to false, so execute short-circuits before the stubbed setting is ever consulted and poll_feed is never called regardless of whether the URL/username guards exist. These examples would still pass if those two guards were deleted. Each example needs the preceding conditions stubbed to their enabling values (enabled true, and a present URL for the username example) so only the guard under test can block polling.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Duplicate downsize definition silently replaces the original API

Ruby does not support method overloading, so the new three-argument self.downsize at line 149 replaces the four-argument self.downsize defined at line 145. Existing callers that pass separate max_width and max_height (optionally with opts) will now raise ArgumentError instead of resizing, while the first definition becomes dead code. Remove the old definition and update all callers, or implement a single signature that handles both dimension forms.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same issue. The duplicate downsize definition overrides the original separate width/height version, which leaves it unreachable and breaks existing callers.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client upload limit is hardcoded and ignores site and file-type settings

validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments could have different configured limits. Replacing it with a constant 10 MB rejects valid uploads on sites configured above 10 MB and accepts attachments or images that the server will later reject on sites configured below 10 MB. The same hardcoded value at line 246 also makes the 413 error message report 10 MB regardless of the actual configured limit.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same problem. The upload limit is hardcoded to 10MB instead of using the per-type site settings, so the client-side limit can diverge from the server's. Both also note that the 413 handler has the same issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage downsizing is passed to gifsicle as an invalid WxH dimension

The controller calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the dimension string "80%", but for animated GIFs downsize_instructions_animated forwards that string to resize_instructions_animated, producing `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. Gifsicle expects a WxH size for --resize-fit (percentage scaling is done with --scale), so the command fails, animated GIFs are not downsized, and the controller retries the failing command five times before the oversized upload is rejected.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: the "80%" value is passed to gifsicle --resize-fit for animated GIFs. That flag expects WxH geometry, so the downsize fails. The candidate adds the retry detail, but the underlying issue is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
Remote-image download cap no longer respects max_image_size_kb

FileHelper.download is now always limited to 10 megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. Sites allowing images larger than 10 MB will fail to fetch otherwise valid remote images, while sites with a smaller limit will download and process needlessly large files before downsizing. The pre-downsize fetch cap should be derived consistently with the client limit and the configured settings.

Downsize failures are ignored while converting the upload in place

OptimizedImage.downsize returns false when conversion or optimization fails, but this loop ignores the result and repeats the operation up to five times on the same tempfile.path used as both source and destination. A failing or partially successful conversion therefore wastes expensive ImageMagick/ImageOptim runs and can leave the only copy of the upload truncated or converted before Upload.create_for consumes it. Convert to a separate temporary output, check the result, and only replace the original after a successful downsize (breaking out of the loop on failure).

No tests cover the new automatic downsizing behavior

The PR adds the downsize loop, changes OptimizedImage.downsize's public signature, and changes client/server size limits, but adds no specs. There is no coverage that an oversized image is reduced below max_image_size_kb, that an image still oversized after five attempts is rejected cleanly, that animated GIFs work, or that existing width/height downsize callers still function, so regressions such as the duplicate downsize definition would not be caught.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row

TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a logged-in user who has never visited or interacted with the topic, for example when an email link is opened while logged in as a different account than the recipient. The next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of creating a TopicUser record at the desired level (as TopicUser.change would) or handling the no-subscription case.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when no record exists, and calling tu.notification_level on it then crashes.

false_positives.candidate: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated-token GET request TopicsController#unsubscribe is exposed as a GET route in config/routes.rb and immediately changes the current user's notification level before rendering the Ember unsubscribe page. A logged-in browser therefore mutates state on any GET, with no confirmation or CSRF token: mail-scanner/link prefetching, a page refresh, or an tag on a third-party site can trigger it. It is also non-idempotent: watching/tracking is first downgraded to regular, and a second visit to the same email link then downgrades regular to muted, so merely reopening the confirmation page further changes the user's settings than the original click intended.

Unsubscribe bypasses the canonical TopicUser.change update path

The action assigns notification_level directly and calls tu.save!, bypassing TopicUser.change (used by TopicsController#set_notifications). TopicUser.change is the path that stamps notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id=user_changed and publishes a MessageBus /topic/:id notification_level_change message. Direct assignment leaves the change metadata stale and means other open clients showing this topic are not updated to the new notification level until reload.

unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url but MessageBuilder provides no fallback

config/locales/server.en.yml changes the shared unsubscribe_link string to interpolate %{unsubscribe_url}, and MessageBuilder#body (line 90) and #html_part (line 67) render that string whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. MessageBuilder supplies defaults for site_name/base_url/user_preferences_url but not unsubscribe_url, and only UserNotifications#send_notification_email passes it. Any other existing caller that builds mail with add_unsubscribe_link: true alone (previously valid, as the old spec did) will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument for unsubscribe_url and fail to send. The builder should only append the per-topic sentence when unsubscribe_url is present, or provide a safe fallback.

New unsubscribe behaviour has no meaningful test coverage

The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" to the message_with_unsubscribe fixture; no example asserts that the per-topic URL actually appears in the text body or HTML part, and the PR adds no controller spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe at all. The slug-mismatch redirect, the watching/tracking->regular and regular->muted transitions, repeat-visit behaviour, anonymous access, and the missing-TopicUser case are therefore all untested and could regress silently.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook helper uses macOS-only sed syntax and still reports success on Linux

The in-place edit uses BSD/macOS syntax 'sed -i '' -E ...'. With GNU sed the empty string is taken as the script, the substitution is treated as a filename, and the edit fails; because the script has no 'set -e' or error check it then prints 'Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL ...' anyway, leaving developers on Linux with a stale or missing webhook URL while believing it was set. The script is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature it ships with.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same problem: the script uses macOS-only sed -i '' syntax, and that fails on Linux. The candidate also mentions the false success message, which is additional detail on top of the same core issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Authorization failure is thrown as a generic Error instead of a TRPCError

When the credential does not belong to the session user the handler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied'). tRPC wraps non-TRPCError throws as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so a client error (unknown or foreign credentialId) is reported and logged as a server failure and callers cannot distinguish it. This should be a TRPCError (e.g. NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN) with an appropriate code.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same problem: an auth or access failure is thrown as a generic Error, which tRPC turns into a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. Both recommend a TRPCError with a proper code such as FORBIDDEN.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp is always formatted in en-US regardless of user locale

The component localizes all strings through useLocale but formats cacheUpdatedAt with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...). Users on non-US locales will see US-style dates/times (e.g. month/day order) in an otherwise localized UI; the formatter should use the user's locale returned by useLocale/i18n.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same problem: the date is formatted with a hardcoded 'en-US' locale when it should use the user's locale from useLocale.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting cache does not invalidate the connected-calendars query

The deleteCache mutation only shows a toast and invokes the optional onSuccess callback, unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on settle. Callers are not required to pass onSuccess (the wrapper forwards an optional prop), so after a successful deletion the connectedCalendars query keeps returning the old cacheUpdatedAt, hasCache stays true, and the UI continues to show the stale timestamp and a Delete action for cache that no longer exists until some unrelated refetch occurs.

Cache status counts expired cache entries as live cache

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups rows by credentialId and returns _max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter. CalendarCache rows are not removed when they expire (getCachedAvailability treats expiresAt < now as a miss, but the row remains), so the new UI will display 'Cache Status / Last updated' and offer Delete for credentials whose only cache rows are already expired and are never actually served.

Unconditional empty updateMany marks every SelectedCalendar for the credential as freshly updated

fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) after the per-event-type loop. The write is unconditional and credential-wide: it bumps updatedAt on every SelectedCalendar row for the credential, including event-type-scoped rows and rows whose calendars were not in the fetched groups, and it runs even when the grouped map is empty and no cache entry was written. Anything reading SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as a freshness marker will be told calendars were refreshed when no cache fetch happened, and every cache population now pays an extra blanket UPDATE.

dev:cron now shells out to unpinned npx tsx, which is not a declared dependency

The script was changed from ts-node (declared in devDependencies) to 'npx tsx cron-tester.ts', but tsx is not declared in apps/web's dependencies. npx will resolve and download whatever latest tsx is available at run time (failing offline and bypassing the lockfile's pinned versions), making the dev script non-reproducible. This unrelated tooling change should either declare tsx as a devDependency or be dropped.

No tests cover the new destructive deleteCache endpoint or cache-status query

The PR adds a destructive, ownership-checked tRPC mutation, a new groupBy repository method, and cache-status enrichment of connectedCalendars, but adds or updates no tests. The security-critical cases are unverified: deleting cache for one's own credential succeeds, deleting another user's credentialId is rejected and deletes nothing, and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns the latest updatedAt per credential. A regression in the findFirst ownership check would let any authenticated user wipe another user's calendar cache without any test failing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours end check uses the slot start instead of the slot end

Both start and end are computed as slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(), so the end > workingHour.endTime comparison never looks at when the proposed booking actually finishes. A 60-minute slot starting at 16:30 in a 09:00-17:00 schedule passes the check even though it ends at 17:30, letting fixed hosts be booked beyond the end of their working hours.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: the end time is computed from slotStartTime when it should come from slotEndTime. The candidate also explains the impact, a slot that runs past working hours still passing the check.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Empty date-override detection compares Dayjs objects with ===

The condition dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false and the intended zero-length override case never triggers. For an 'unavailable' date override where start equals end, a slot straddling that instant satisfies neither the before-start nor after-end branch, so the function falls through to returning true and offers a slot on a day the host marked unavailable.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same bug: comparing two dayjs objects with === checks object references, so the result is always false. The candidate explains this and the downstream consequence for unavailable date overrides.

false_positives.candidate:
Slots inside a date override bypass the busy-time check

In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot's date matches a date override and the slot is inside the override window, the function returns true immediately. It never reaches the busy.every(...) check against existing Cal bookings and connected-calendar busy times. A fixed or round-robin host who has a date override on a day can therefore be shown as available at times when they already have a booking or calendar event, allowing double-bookings on override days.

Only the first same-day date override is considered

The dateOverrides.find(...) callback returns true as soon as the slot falls outside the first override that shares the slot's date. If a user has two override ranges on the same day (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00, which Cal.com allows as separate availability rows), a slot inside the second range is judged against the first range, find() stops, and checkIfIsAvailable returns false. Valid slots in the second and later override ranges of the day are incorrectly removed, notably for fixed hosts in round-robin events.

Override containment check admits partially overlapping slots

A slot is treated as inside a date override unless its end is at/before the override start or its start is strictly after the override end. A slot that starts before the override begins but ends inside it (e.g. 13:30-14:30 for a 14:00-18:00 override) is not flagged as outside and is reported available, and a slot starting exactly at the override end is also treated as inside because isAfter is used instead of isSameOrAfter. Bookings can therefore start before the host's override availability begins or exactly when it ends.

Working-hours gate is wrong for split schedules and days off

The workingHours.find(...) check returns 'outside working hours' if ANY working-hour entry for that weekday does not cover the slot, so a host with split hours (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on the same day) has afternoon slots rejected because the morning entry does not cover them. Conversely, if no entry lists the slot's weekday at all, find() returns nothing and the check passes entirely, so a fixed host can still be booked on a day off whenever a round-robin host's availability generated that slot. Both cases defeat the fixed-host enforcement this block was added for.

Timezone-shifted override can be assigned to the wrong invitee day

The new code converts the override wall time by the invitee-minus-organizer offset and keeps only hour/minute, discarding the resulting date, while the activeOverrides filter above still selects overrides by comparing the unshifted UTC-encoded start against the invitee day. For an organizer ahead of the invitee (e.g. a 09:00 override in UTC+10 viewed from UTC), the converted time is 23:00 on the previous invitee day, but the filter attaches it to the following invitee day, so the slot is offered a day late instead of on the correct day.

No test covers the fixed-host round-robin override scenario

The PR description states the main fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts restrict round-robin events, but the only added test re-queries a personal (non-team) event in Asia/Dhaka versus Asia/Kolkata and expects identical UTC slots. Nothing exercises a ROUND_ROBIN event type with an isFixed host who has a date override, the new checkIfIsAvailable override/working-hours paths for fixed and loose hosts, or a timezone change that crosses a date boundary, so regressions in the primary claimed behavior would go undetected.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry increments use a stale read instead of an atomic increment

Both retry paths set retryCount to reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value fetched at the start of the cron run. Overlapping cron invocations, which are possible while this handler sequentially makes slow Twilio calls, can read the same count, both fail, and both write the same incremented value, losing failures and keeping bad reminders alive beyond the intended two failures. Use Prisma's atomic data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } operation instead.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same issue. Setting retryCount from a stale read (reminder.retryCount + 1) loses increments under concurrency, and the fix is Prisma's atomic increment. Both also apply this to both retry paths.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry-based deletion is not scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders

The second OR branch matches any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or scheduled state. It can therefore delete EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders and, if an SMS reminder reaches retryCount 2 while also becoming scheduled, delete a reminder already scheduled with Twilio. Deleting the scheduled row removes the referenceId needed to cancel that Twilio message if the booking is cancelled or rescheduled, so the SMS can still be delivered. Scope this branch to method SMS and scheduled: false.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same problem. The retryCount > 1 OR branch has no SMS method filter, so it can delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders. It also suggests scoping the branch to method SMS. Its added points about scheduled state go beyond the golden comment but do not change the core match.

false_positives.candidate:
Reminders with no recipient or message never accrue retries

Scheduling, the retry increment for a null Twilio result, and error handling only occur when both message and sendTo are truthy. A reminder whose booking has no smsReminderNumber/sendTo, or whose generated message is empty, remains scheduled:false with retryCount 0 and is fetched again on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes, which is the retry loop this PR is meant to eliminate. Such permanently unschedulable reminders should increment retryCount or otherwise be logged and eventually removed.

Unguarded retry update in catch can abort the whole cron run

The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without its own error handling. If that update rejects, for example because the row was deleted concurrently, the database is transiently unavailable, or the original exception came from a workflowReminder update, the exception escapes the per-reminder loop and handler. All remaining unscheduled reminders are then skipped for that run and the endpoint errors instead of continuing as the previous log-and-continue behavior did. The increment should be best-effort and not abort processing of subsequent reminders.

No tests cover the new retry and deletion state machine

The PR adds retry increments on Twilio-null and exception paths and deletion when retryCount exceeds 1, but adds no automated tests. There is no coverage proving that a failure increments once, a successful schedule does not get deleted, reminders are removed only after the intended number of failures, or one reminder's failure does not prevent later reminders from being processed. Add handler tests with mocked Prisma and Twilio for these cases.

findMany is removed without migrating production callers

The public findMany method is replaced by getBaseConditions, and getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions now return Prisma.Sql instead of Prisma WhereInput objects. The PR changes only this service and its test, with no production caller migrated to $queryRaw with getBaseConditions. Any existing caller using service.findMany or passing the returned conditions into a Prisma where clause will fail TypeScript compilation; all such call sites must be migrated in this PR or a compatibility adapter retained.

Event-type filter returns an unparenthesized OR fragment

When eventTypeId is the only filter, buildFilterConditions returns `("eventTypeId" = ...) OR ("eventParentId" = ...)` without outer parentheses. If a caller composes it naturally as `WHERE ${authConditions} AND ${filterConditions}`, PostgreSQL precedence parses it as `(auth AND eventTypeId = ...) OR (eventParentId = ...)`, allowing the eventParentId branch to bypass the authorization conditions. getBaseConditions happens to wrap the fragment, but the public getFilterConditions result no longer guarantees the grouping that the previous Prisma WhereInput object provided; the predicate itself should be wrapped in parentheses.

The org and team authorization tests only compare Prisma.Sql objects constructed with the same template helper as the implementation, while the sole $queryRaw execution in the suite uses user scope with scalar userId/teamId predicates. referencesToCreate now sets credentialId to result.credentialId only for calendar results and to undefined for everything else. Previously video results kept result.credentialId. Booking references for video meetings are consequently persisted without a credentialId, and later flows that look up the specific video credential from the reference (e.g. cancellation deleting the meeting only when reference.credentialId is present) can no longer find/delete the meeting, leaving orphaned video meetings.

updateLocation creates booking references with no calendar/credential identifiers

updateLocation now builds references from result.externalId and result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent's returned EventResult never populates either field (its return object contains only appName/type/success/uid/updatedEvent/originalEvent/calError/calWarnings). editLocation.handler persists these referencesToCreate, so after a location change the booking's calendar references have externalCalendarId and credentialId undefined, breaking subsequent updates/cancellations that need them to address the correct host calendar.

Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event

When newBookingId is supplied, the cleanup uses booking.references.find(...) to locate a single old calendar reference and deletes only that event. Bookings created by this PR can have one reference per collective host, so the old events on all other hosts' calendars are left behind as orphaned/stale events after a reschedule merge.

Confirming a collective booking only creates the organizer's calendar event

The confirmation path rebuilds the CalendarEvent with only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar as a one-element array; the other collective hosts' destination calendars stored at booking time are not reconstructed (the Booking row itself only persists the first one). Since calendar events for requiresConfirmation bookings are created on confirmation via handleConfirmation/EventManager.create, the non-organizer hosts will not receive calendar events for confirmed collective bookings, which is the scenario this PR sets out to fix. The same single-calendar reconstruction exists in the Stripe/PayPal payment-success handlers.

Webhook payload shape for destinationCalendar changes and is inconsistent

CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changes from a DestinationCalendar object/null to an array, and CalendarEvent objects are spread directly into webhook payloads. External consumers (webhooks/Zapier) that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId will break. The value is also now inconsistent for 'no destination': handleNewBooking emits null while confirm/cancel/payment flows emit [], so consumers cannot rely on a single shape; only one of the three webhook e2e expectations was updated to match.

false_negatives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited and outside try/catch

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) returns immediately, so Reschedule proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before getCalendar and deleteEvent/deleteMeeting finish. Rejections from the async callback are not caught by the surrounding try/catch and become unhandled rejections, and on serverless runtimes the deletions may never complete after the response returns. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) so deletions finish and errors are handled before continuing.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: forEach with async callbacks leaves the calendar/video deletions unawaited. Both note that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch the rejections, which become unhandled. Both recommend Promise.all with map as the fix.

false_positives.candidate:
Dynamic imports are all started eagerly, defeating lazy loading

Every value in the appStore object literal is an already-invoked import() call, so importing this module immediately starts loading all 28 app packages and their dependencies, even when the caller only needs one app. This defeats the intended on-demand loading, and because most of these promises are never awaited for a given request, a rejection from an unused optional app can surface as an unhandled promise rejection instead of being handled by the code that selected that app. Store lazy thunks such as () => import(...) or otherwise create the import only for the requested key.

Async forEach races reschedule email/webhook against booking deletions

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) is not awaited, so the requestReschedule mutation immediately sends the reschedule email and webhooks while calendar/video deletion for the old booking is still pending at the dynamic-import step. The deletions can be lost if execution is frozen after the mutation returns, and failures become unhandled rejections rather than being surfaced or logged. Await Promise.all over a map of the deletion operations before sending the email/webhooks.

Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it is awaited

The recurring-cancellation branch uses credentials.forEach(async ...) and pushes into apiDeletes only after awaiting getCalendar and calendar.deleteEvent. Because the forEach is never awaited, the handler reaches Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at the end (and the earlier await apiDeletes in the paid path) before those pushes happen, so recurring calendar events are not reliably deleted before attendee/booking-reference rows are removed and the cancellation response is sent. Replace the forEach with an awaited for...of loop or await Promise.all(map(...)) that fills apiDeletes before it is consumed.
